docs.content:
Question: Can I return to Cartagena on a different day?
Other ways to ask: How do I stay extra days on the island? / Is return on a different date included?
Answer: Returning to Cartagena on a different date from the plan is not included. If the guest wants to stay longer on the islands and come back with us another day, a member of our team arranges it (space on the boat, etc.).

Question: Do 2-day courses require staying overnight on the islands?
Other ways to ask: Is it mandatory to stay overnight on the islands for 2-day courses? / Can I do the Open Water or Advanced course without staying on the islands?
Answer: Yes. Courses that last 2 days (such as Open Water and Advanced) require accommodation on the Rosario Islands. There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days, as the second day's itinerary starts directly on the islands. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel.

Question: Can you pick me up if I'm already on the Rosario Islands?
Other ways to ask: How does transport work from my hotel on the islands? / Is the price different if I'm picked up on the island?
Answer: If you are already on the Rosario Islands, we coordinate pick-up and drop-off from hotels with maritime access. In some cases the boat arrives directly at the hotel; in others we indicate the nearest dock or meeting point. These plans have different prices because they do not include transport from Cartagena or lunch.

Question: If I'm already on the Rosario Islands, can you pick me up at my hotel?
Other ways to ask: Can you pick me up at my hotel if I'm already staying on the islands? / Is hotel pick-up included if I'm staying on the Rosario Islands?
Answer: Yes. If you are already on the Rosario Islands and your hotel has maritime access, pick-up and return by boat are included at no extra charge. In some cases, the boat arrives directly at the hotel; in others, a team advisor will indicate the nearest dock or meeting point. These plans have different prices because they do not include transport from Cartagena or lunch.

Question: Do I need to stay on the islands for the course?
Other ways to ask: Can I commute from Cartagena each day of the course? / Is accommodation included in the course?
Answer: Two-day courses (Open Water, Advanced) require accommodation on the islands. There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel.

Service sheet: Open Water Referral Course — departing from Cartagena

If you already completed the theory and pool sessions at your local PADI center, you can finish your Open Water certification in 2 days while diving in the Rosario Islands.

Facts for Open Water Referral Course: 474 USD / 1.680.000 COP online, 526 USD / 1.867.000 COP regular; 2 days; on day 1 you can return to Cartagena or stay on the islands (lodging not included); boat Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena included; lunch on day 1 only; no prior certification.

Included for Open Water Referral Course:
- Entry to the Rosario Islands Natural Park
- Mandatory dive insurance
- Roundtrip boat transfer Cartagena-Islands
- 4 certification dives with a PADI instructor
- Full diving equipment
- Surface intervals with access to hotel facilities
- Lunch on day 1
- PADI certification
- Eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL

Not included for Open Water Referral Course:
- Ground transportation to the dock
- Hotel/accommodation on the Rosario Islands
- Underwater photos or videos
- Voluntary tips
- Additional food beyond the included lunch
- Any other service not specified

Itinerary for Open Water Referral Course:
- Phase 1: theory + pool sessions completed at your home PADI dive center
- Day 1: meeting point at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. + referral paperwork check
- Day 1: speedboat transfer to the Rosario Islands (approx. 1 hour)
- Day 1: welcome at our base + theory review + equipment check
- Day 1: 2 certification dives + lunch (included)
- Day 1: activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.; option to return to Cartagena (like the other plans: departure 3:00 p.m., estimated arrival 4:15 p.m.) or stay overnight on the islands (hotel not included)
- Day 2: 2 final dives + lunch (not included)
- Day 2: return to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (estimated arrival 4:15 p.m.) + certification processing

Requirements for Open Water Referral Course:
- Have completed the theory and pool sessions at your home PADI dive center
- Bring your referral paperwork signed by a PADI instructor
- After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying

Before the activity for Open Water Referral Course: You must arrive with the theory and pool sessions completed at your home dive center and bring your referral paperwork signed by a PADI instructor.

More info: https://divingplanet.org/curso-padi-cartagena/referido/

Service sheet: PADI Basic Course (Open Water) — departing from Cartagena

PADI Open Water course with online theory (eLearning) and practical training in the Rosario Islands: pool sessions + 4 certification dives.

Facts for PADI Basic Course (Open Water): 693 USD / 2.450.000 COP online, 770 USD / 2.722.000 COP regular; 2 days; you must stay overnight on the islands (lodging not included), not a same-day round trip; boat Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena included; lunch on day 1 only; no prior certification.

Included for PADI Basic Course (Open Water):
- National Park entrance fee
- Mandatory dive insurance
- Speedboat transport Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena
- Pool training + 4 certification dives with a PADI instructor
- Diving equipment for the practical sessions
- Lunch on day 1
- PADI certification card
- Eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL

Not included for PADI Basic Course (Open Water):
- Ground transportation to the dock
- Hotel/accommodation on the Rosario Islands
- Underwater photos or videos
- Voluntary tips
- Additional food beyond the included lunch
- Any other service not specified

Itinerary for PADI Basic Course (Open Water):
- Phase 1: online theory (PADI eLearning)
- Day 1: meeting point at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. + speedboat transfer (approx. 1 hour)
- Day 1: welcome at our island base + equipment check + pool (confined water)
- Day 1: 2 certification dives + surface interval + lunch (included)
- Day 1: activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.; then transfer to the hotel where you'll stay overnight (hotel not included)
- Day 2: second pool session + 2 final dives
- Day 2: lunch (not included) + return to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (estimated arrival 4:15 p.m.)
- Day 2: PADI Open Water Diver certification processing

Requirements for PADI Basic Course (Open Water):
- With this plan you must stay at least 1 night on the Rosario Islands (hotel not included)
- After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying

Before the activity for PADI Basic Course (Open Water): The theory is done through PADI eLearning (approx. 10 to 12 hours). You must complete it before starting the practical phase.

Booking: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/basic-course/4?language=es · More info: https://divingplanet.org/curso-padi-cartagena/basico-open-water/

Service sheet: PADI Advanced Course — departing from Cartagena

PADI Advanced Open Water course with prior theory and 5 dives with an instructor. Includes a night dive and 1 night on the islands (hotel not included).

Facts for PADI Advanced Course: 616 USD / 2.175.000 COP online, 685 USD / 2.417.000 COP regular; 2 days; includes a night dive; you must stay overnight on the islands (lodging not included), not a same-day round trip; boat Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena included; lunch on day 1 only; certification required.

Included for PADI Advanced Course:
- Online course/digital materials access
- National Park entrance fee
- Mandatory dive insurance
- Speedboat transport Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena
- Theory sessions before each dive
- 5 dives with a certified PADI instructor
- Full diving equipment
- Lunch on day 1
- PADI certification card
- Eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL

Not included for PADI Advanced Course:
- Ground transportation to the dock
- Hotel/accommodation on the Rosario Islands
- Underwater photos or videos
- Voluntary tips
- Additional food beyond the included lunch
- Any other service not specified

Itinerary for PADI Advanced Course:
- Phase 1: theory (digital materials + knowledge reviews)
- Day 1: meeting point at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. + speedboat transfer (approx. 1 hour)
- Day 1: arrival at the island base + theory review + equipment setup
- Day 1: 2 specialty dives + lunch (included) + theory review
- Day 1: night dive + transfer to the hotel (hotel not included)
- Day 2: 2 additional specialty dives + lunch (not included)
- Day 2: return to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (estimated arrival 4:15 p.m.) + certification processing

Requirements for PADI Advanced Course:
- With this plan you must stay at least 1 night on the Rosario Islands (hotel not included)
- After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying

Before the activity for PADI Advanced Course: After enrollment you'll receive digital materials/course access. It's important to complete the knowledge reviews before the dives.

Booking: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/advanced-course/5?language=es · More info: https://divingplanet.org/curso-padi-cartagena/avanzado/

- Day 1: meeting point at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. + speedboat transfer (approx. 1 hour)
- Day 1: welcome at our island base + equipment check + pool (confined water)
- Day 1: 2 certification dives + surface interval + lunch (included)
- Day 1: activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.; then transfer to the hotel where you'll stay overnight (hotel not included)
- Day 2: second pool session + 2 final dives
- Day 2: lunch (not included) + return to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (estimated arrival 4:15 p.m.)
- Day 2: PADI Open Water Diver certification processing

- With this plan you must stay at least 1 night on the Rosario Islands (hotel not included)

docs.content:
Pregunta: ¿Qué comida incluye el tour?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Qué tipo de comida ofrecen durante el tour? / ¿El almuerzo está incluido en la actividad de buceo o snorkel?
Respuesta: El tour incluye agua durante todo el día, dulces de coco entre inmersiones y almuerzo (arroz con pollo o arroz con vegetales). Los vegetarianos, veganos y celíacos reciben arroz con vegetales. Si tienes alguna alergia alimentaria, debes informarlo antes del tour. El almuerzo solo está incluido el primer día para quienes salen desde Cartagena; para quienes ya están en las islas, el almuerzo no está incluido.

Pregunta: ¿Qué incluye el tour?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Qué servicios están incluidos en el tour? / ¿Qué recibo al reservar un tour con ustedes?
Respuesta: Todos los tours incluyen: entrada al Parque Nacional, seguro de buceo, transporte en lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena (si la salida es desde Cartagena), equipo completo y aporte eco-social a DIVE TO HEAL. El almuerzo está incluido solo el primer día para quienes salen desde Cartagena. Si ya estás en las Islas del Rosario, el almuerzo no está incluido.

Pregunta: ¿Snorkel y buceo van juntos en la lancha?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Se separan los grupos de snorkel y buceo? / ¿Dónde se hace el snorkel si voy con buzos?
Respuesta: En los grupos que combinan buceo y snorkel, el snorkel se hace en una zona distinta a la del buceo. Si hay poca gente van juntos en la misma lancha; si no, se dividen por actividad.

Plan de snorkeling para disfrutar del arrecife desde la superficie: 2 salidas guiadas con un guia local y almuerzo en las islas.

Datos de Tour de Snorkeling: 126 USD / 448.000 COP online, 140 USD / 497.000 COP normal; 1 día; ida y vuelta desde Cartagena el mismo día; lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena incluida; almuerzo incluido; sin certificación previa; edad mínima 6.

Incluye de Tour de Snorkeling:
- Tarifa de ingreso al Parque Nacional Natural
- Seguro de la actividad
- Transporte en lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena
- 2 salidas guiadas con guia local

- Almuerzo

- Almuerzo en las instalaciones del hotel

Pregunta: ¿Pueden venir grupos con diferentes niveles (certificados, principiantes y snorkeling) en el mismo tour?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Se pueden mezclar buzos certificados, principiantes y personas que solo hacen snorkel en el mismo tour? / ¿Un grupo con diferentes niveles de experiencia puede hacer actividades juntos en el mismo día?
Respuesta: Sí, es posible combinar diferentes actividades en un solo tour. Los grupos pueden estar formados por buzos certificados, personas que desean realizar el minicurso y quienes solo quieren hacer snorkeling. Mientras los buzos certificados realizan su primera inmersión o los snorkelers su primera actividad, los participantes del minicurso hacen su entrenamiento teórico y práctico en piscina. En la segunda inmersión, si lo desean, pueden unirse con los del minicurso para la inmersión en aguas abiertas. En los grupos que combinan buceo y snorkel, el snorkel se realiza en una zona distinta a la del buceo. Si hay poca gente, van juntos en la misma lancha; si no, se dividen por actividad. Más información: https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/

Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Qué plan es el más adecuado para mí? / ¿Qué opciones tienen según si soy buzo certificado o principiante?
Respuesta: La recomendación depende de tu experiencia y lo que buscas: si eres buzo certificado, hay salidas de buceo recreativo y paquetes para diferentes niveles; si eres principiante, puedes optar por el minicurso de buceo (bautizo); también ofrecemos cursos PADI y tours de snorkeling. Un asesor del equipo puede orientarte sobre el plan más adecuado según tu perfil.

Pregunta: ¿Está el seguro incluido en la actividad?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿El seguro está cubierto en los tours de buceo o snorkel? / ¿Debo pagar un seguro adicional para bucear o hacer snorkel?
Respuesta: Sí, el seguro de la actividad (buceo o snorkel) está incluido en todos los planes y tours, tanto saliendo desde Cartagena como para quienes ya están en las Islas del Rosario. No es necesario pagar nada adicional ni contratar un seguro por cuenta propia. Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que se envía en el correo de confirmación.

Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Dónde encuentro información para reservar el tour de snorkeling? / ¿Cómo puedo consultar el plan de snorkeling y hacer la reserva?
Respuesta: Puedes ver los detalles y reservar el Tour de Snorkeling en este enlace: https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/tour-snorkeling/

- Salida a Islas del Rosario (aprox. 1 hora)

- Despues de bucear, esperar minimo 18 horas antes de tomar un vuelo

Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿El seguro está cubierto en los tours de buceo o snorkel? / ¿Debo pagar un seguro adicional para bucear o hacer snorkel?
Respuesta: Sí, el seguro de la actividad (buceo o snorkel) está incluido en todos los planes y tours, tanto saliendo desde Cartagena como para quienes ya están en las Islas del Rosario. No es necesario pagar nada adicional ni contratar un seguro por cuenta propia. Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que se envía en el correo de confirmación.

[5] Fuente: policies
Pregunta: ¿Cómo funciona el descuento para grupos?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿El descuento de grupo se aplica automáticamente al reservar online? / ¿Qué tengo que hacer para obtener el 20% de descuento si somos 5 o más?
Respuesta: 10% de descuento para grupos de 5 personas o más, que se suma al 10% de descuento online (20% total reservando online). No aplica automáticamente: el grupo debe contactar al equipo para aplicarlo. No aplica a cursos PADI.

[6] Fuente: faqs
Pregunta: ¿Puede venir un acompañante que no bucea?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Mi pareja puede ir en la lancha aunque no se sumerja? / ¿Qué incluye el plan de acompañante? / ¿Cuánto paga alguien que solo acompaña?
Respuesta: Sí. El plan de acompañante es para quien no bucea ni hace snorkel y va en la lancha con el grupo. Saliendo desde Cartagena incluye la lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena, el almuerzo, el seguro y la entrada al Parque Nacional Natural. Si ya están en las islas, el acompañante va en la lancha con el grupo e incluye el seguro y la entrada al Parque Nacional Natural; el almuerzo no está incluido. El precio es el mismo saliendo desde Cartagena o ya en las islas (el del catálogo, con el 10 % de descuento online).

[7] Fuente: policies
Pregunta: ¿Hay descuento si llevo mi propio equipo?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿El 5% aplica si solo llevo parte del equipo? / ¿Qué necesito traer para obtener el descuento por equipo propio?
Respuesta: 5% de descuento si el cliente trae su propio equipo COMPLETO (regulador, BCD/chaleco, traje, máscara, aletas, etc.). No aplica si solo trae parte del equipo.

[8] Fuente: faqs
Pregunta: ¿Puedo hacer una inmersión extra además de mi paquete?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Se puede añadir una inmersión adicional a mi paquete de buceo? / ¿Hay posibilidad de hacer una inmersión extra si ya tengo un paquete?

Desde Cartagena no está disponible por esta misma razón. La disponibilidad real debe ser confirmada por un asesor del equipo antes de asumir que es posible.

Question: Can I bring a suitcase on the boat?
Other ways to ask: Is there somewhere to store my luggage? / Is it just one bag per person?
Answer: Each person can bring one backpack or bag on the boat. If the guest needs to bring a suitcase, it has to be arranged with a member of our team. If they prefer not to take it, we can store the suitcase at our office in Cartagena.

Question: Do you have accommodation options in the Rosario Islands?
Other ways to ask: Where can I stay if I go diving with you in the Rosario Islands? / Is accommodation included in the diving plans or do I need to book it separately?
Answer: Our dive base is located at two hotels: Hotel San Pedro de Majagua and Hotel Cocoliso, both on Isla Grande (Rosario Islands). You can stay at either of these hotels for greater convenience, but it is not required. You may also choose other hotels in the area with maritime access or a nearby dock, such as Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras, and Pao Pao. Accommodation is not included in the diving plans and must be booked directly with the hotel.

- National Park entrance fee
- Mandatory dive insurance
- Speedboat transport Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena
- 5 guided dives with a certified PADI professional
- Diving equipment
- Lunch on day 1
- Eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL

- Lunches not explicitly included

- Additional food beyond the included lunch
- Any other service not specified

- Day 1: 2 dives + surface interval + lunch (included)
- Day 1: 1 night dive

- Day 2: lunch (not included)

- With this plan you must stay 1 night on the Rosario Islands (hotel not included)
- After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying

Question: What recommendations should I follow for a diving day in the Rosario Islands?
Other ways to ask: What should I bring or keep in mind for diving in the Rosario Islands? / Any practical tips for a diving day in the islands?
Answer: It is recommended to bring reef-safe sunscreen, stay hydrated throughout the day, use sunglasses and sun protection, and consider seasickness tablets if you are sensitive to boats. An underwater camera can be useful if you want photos of reefs and fish. For the water, light tropical exposure protection is usually enough because the temperature is around 28°C, although everyone tolerates cold differently. It is important not to touch coral or wildlife, maintain good buoyancy, and always follow the guide or instructor's directions.

Question: What recommendations should I follow for a diving day in the Rosario Islands?
Other ways to ask: What should I bring or keep in mind for diving in the Rosario Islands? / Any practical tips for a diving day in the islands?
Answer: It is recommended to bring reef-safe sunscreen, stay hydrated throughout the day, use sunglasses and sun protection, and consider seasickness tablets if you are sensitive to boats. An underwater camera can be useful if you want photos of reefs and fish. For the water, light tropical exposure protection is usually enough because the temperature is around 28°C, although everyone tolerates cold differently. It is important not to touch coral or wildlife, maintain good buoyancy, and always follow the guide or instructor's directions.

docs.content:
Pregunta: ¿Qué no está incluido?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cuáles son los servicios que no están cubiertos en el plan? / ¿Qué gastos adicionales debo considerar que no están incluidos?
Respuesta: No está incluido: transporte terrestre al muelle, fotos y videos submarinos, propinas voluntarias, comida adicional al almuerzo, y el regreso a Cartagena en una fecha distinta a la del plan. Si el cliente desea regresar en una fecha diferente, lo coordina un asesor del equipo.

Pregunta: ¿Qué comida incluye el tour?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Qué tipo de comida ofrecen durante el tour? / ¿El almuerzo está incluido en la actividad de buceo o snorkel?
Respuesta: El tour incluye agua durante todo el día, dulces de coco entre inmersiones y almuerzo (arroz con pollo o arroz con vegetales). Los vegetarianos, veganos y celíacos reciben arroz con vegetales. Si tienes alguna alergia alimentaria, debes informarlo antes del tour. El almuerzo solo está incluido el primer día para quienes salen desde Cartagena; para quienes ya están en las islas, el almuerzo no está incluido.

Ficha del servicio: Servicio Privado — saliendo desde Cartagena

Datos de Servicio Privado: precio: lo cotiza un asesor; almuerzo NO incluido; sin certificación previa.

Más información: https://divingplanet.org/servicio-privado-buceo-cartagena/

Pregunta: ¿Qué incluye el tour?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Qué servicios están incluidos en el tour? / ¿Qué recibo al reservar un tour con ustedes?
Respuesta: Todos los tours incluyen: entrada al Parque Nacional, seguro de buceo, transporte en lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena (si la salida es desde Cartagena), equipo completo y aporte eco-social a DIVE TO HEAL. El almuerzo está incluido solo el primer día para quienes salen desde Cartagena. Si ya estás en las Islas del Rosario, el almuerzo no está incluido.

Pregunta: ¿Puede venir un acompañante que no bucea?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Mi pareja puede ir en la lancha aunque no se sumerja? / ¿Qué incluye el plan de acompañante? / ¿Cuánto paga alguien que solo acompaña?
Respuesta: Sí. El plan de acompañante es para quien no bucea ni hace snorkel y va en la lancha con el grupo. Saliendo desde Cartagena incluye la lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena, el almuerzo, el seguro y la entrada al Parque Nacional Natural. Si ya están en las islas, el acompañante va en la lancha con el grupo e incluye el seguro y la entrada al Parque Nacional Natural; el almuerzo no está incluido. El precio es el mismo saliendo desde Cartagena o ya en las islas (el del catálogo, con el 10 % de descuento online).

Pregunta: ¿Puedo regresar a Cartagena otro día?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cómo hago si quiero quedarme más días en la isla? / ¿El regreso en fecha diferente está incluido?
Respuesta: El regreso a Cartagena en una fecha distinta a la del plan no está incluido. Si el cliente quiere quedarse más días en las islas y volver con nosotros otro día, lo coordina un asesor del equipo (espacio en la lancha, etc.).

Ficha del servicio: Tour de Snorkeling — saliendo desde Cartagena

Plan de snorkeling para disfrutar del arrecife desde la superficie: 2 salidas guiadas con un guia local y almuerzo en las islas.

Datos de Tour de Snorkeling: 126 USD / 448.000 COP online, 140 USD / 497.000 COP normal; 1 día; ida y vuelta desde Cartagena el mismo día; lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena incluida; almuerzo incluido; sin certificación previa; edad mínima 6.

Incluye de Tour de Snorkeling:
- Tarifa de ingreso al Parque Nacional Natural
- Seguro de la actividad
- Transporte en lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena
- 2 salidas guiadas con guia local
- Equipo de snorkeling
- Almuerzo
- Aporte eco-social a DIVE TO HEAL

No incluye de Tour de Snorkeling:
- Transporte terrestre al muelle
- Fotos o videos
- Propinas voluntarias
- Comida adicional diferente al almuerzo incluido
- Regreso en una fecha distinta a la programada

Itinerario de Tour de Snorkeling:
- Punto de encuentro: Muelle de la Bodeguita a las 8:00 a.m. (a 5 min del centro historico)
- Traslado en lancha rapida (aprox. 1 hora) a las Islas del Rosario
- Bienvenida en nuestra base en las islas
- Entrega de equipo de snorkeling
- 2 salidas guiadas de snorkel + intervalo de superficie
- Almuerzo en las instalaciones del hotel
- Regreso a Cartagena a las 3:00 p.m. (llegada estimada 4:15 p.m.)

Requisitos de Tour de Snorkeling:
- Llegar puntual al punto de encuentro (8:00 a.m.)
- Edad mínima: 6 años

Reserva: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/superficio/3?language=es · Más información: https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/tour-snorkeling/

Pregunta: ¿Si ya estoy en las Islas del Rosario, me recogen en mi hotel?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Pueden recogerme en mi hotel si ya estoy en las islas? / ¿La recogida en el hotel está incluida si me hospedo en las Islas del Rosario?
Respuesta: Sí. Si ya estás en las Islas del Rosario y tu hotel tiene acceso marítimo, la recogida y el regreso en lancha están incluidos sin cargo adicional. En algunos casos la lancha llega directo al hotel; en otros, un asesor del equipo te indica el muelle o punto más cercano. Estos planes tienen precios diferentes porque no incluyen transporte desde Cartagena ni almuerzo.

docs.content:
Question: I'm vegetarian or have a food allergy. Can you accommodate me?
Other ways to ask: What food options do you have for vegetarians, vegans, or people with allergies? / Can I bring my own food if I have a special diet or allergies?
Answer: Yes. Vegetarians, vegans, and celiacs receive rice with vegetables for lunch. If you have a specific allergy (shellfish, gluten, nuts, etc.) or prefer to bring your own food, you're welcome to do so; just let us know before the tour so we can manage it. If you are already on the islands, lunch is not included in the plan.

Question: What food is included in the tour?
Other ways to ask: Can I bring my own food? / Do you have options for vegetarians or people with allergies?
Answer: The tour includes water all day, coconut candy between dives, and lunch (rice with chicken or rice with vegetables). The menu is always the same, it does not change by day/supplier. Vegetarians, vegans, and celiacs receive rice with vegetables. Guests may bring their own food if needed (e.g. allergy or special diet). If the guest has a food allergy, they must inform us before the tour.

Question: What food is included in the tour?
Other ways to ask: What kind of food is offered during the tour? / Is lunch included in the diving or snorkeling activity?
Answer: The tour includes water throughout the day, coconut candy between dives, and lunch (rice with chicken or rice with vegetables). Vegetarians, vegans, and those with celiac disease receive rice with vegetables. If you have any food allergy, you must inform us before the tour. Lunch is only included on the first day for those departing from Cartagena; for those already on the islands, lunch is not included.

Question: If I stay at Pao Pao, San Pedro de Majagua, or Cocoliso, can you pick me up?
Other ways to ask: Do you pick up at Pao Pao, San Pedro de Majagua, or Cocoliso hotel? / Can you arrange pick-up if I stay at Pao Pao, Majagua, or Cocoliso?
Answer: Yes. San Pedro de Majagua and Cocoliso are our island base, so pick-up there is confirmed. For Pao Pao, pick-up is also coordinated, but a team advisor needs to confirm the logistics with you first: depending on the hotel's maritime access, the boat may arrive directly or you may need to walk a short distance to the nearest dock. The exact pick-up point and time will be confirmed by a team advisor, who will also ask for your hotel name to coordinate it.

Question: Can I bring a suitcase on the boat?
Other ways to ask: Is there somewhere to store my luggage? / Is it just one bag per person?
Answer: Each person can bring one backpack or bag on the boat. If the guest needs to bring a suitcase, it has to be arranged with a member of our team. If they prefer not to take it, we can store the suitcase at our office in Cartagena.

Question: Do I need to show my diver card to join?
Other ways to ask: Can I send you a picture of my certification? / What if I forget my diver card?
Answer: For recreational dive outings, you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.

Question: Do you offer private or closed group services?
Other ways to ask: How much does a private tour cost? / Can I book just for my group?
Answer: Private services and closed groups are available, with no fixed price (it depends on the group and the date). A member of our team prepares the quote and coordinates an available instructor for the date.

Question: Can I reschedule my booking?
Other ways to ask: How do I change the date of my dive? / What if I need to move my reservation to another day?
Answer: Date changes are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/

docs.content:
Question: Does the mini-course give certification?
Other ways to ask: Do I need anything from PADI for the mini-course? / What's included in the try-dive?
Answer: The mini-course is a one-day try-dive, an introduction to diving: it does not certify, does not count as part of any PADI course and requires nothing from PADI beforehand (no PADI account or PADI online course). After booking you receive the theory part by email, which must be completed before the activity; the day includes pool practice and 1 ocean dive with an instructor.

Question: What's the minimum age for diving?
Other ways to ask: Can kids join the activities? / From what age can you do the mini course?
Answer: It depends on the activity: snorkeling from 6 years old; Bubble Makers from 8 to 10 years old (pool mini-course and very shallow water practice, max 2 meters); the dive mini-course and PADI courses from 10 years old. Minors must be accompanied by a demonstrable parent or responsible relative.

Question: What is the minimum age to participate?
Other ways to ask: From what age can children participate? / What is the minimum age for each diving or snorkeling activity?
Answer: The minimum age depends on the activity: for snorkeling, from 6 years old; for Bubble Makers, from 8 to 10 years old (mini-course in a pool and very shallow water, maximum 2 meters); for the dive mini-course and PADI courses, from 10 years old. Minors must be accompanied by a demonstrable parent or responsible relative.

Question: What is the maximum allowed diving depth?
Other ways to ask: How deep can I dive according to my certification? / What is the depth limit for each diving level?
Answer: The maximum depth depends on your level and always respects the limit of each certification: the mini-course or discover scuba allows up to 12 meters (typically between 5 and 12 meters); certified Open Water divers can go up to 18 meters; divers with Advanced certification (and advanced packages) up to 30 meters; the Bubble Makers program for children ages 8 to 10 reaches 2 meters. The actual depth of each dive depends on the selected dive site, always within your certification limit.

Question: What is the Bubble Makers program?
Other ways to ask: How does Bubble Makers work for kids? / From what age can children participate in Bubble Makers?
Answer: Bubble Makers is a PADI program designed for children ages 8 to 10 who want to safely try diving. The activity takes place in a pool or very shallow water (maximum 2 meters deep), always with a PADI instructor dedicated exclusively to them. It is the way for children of that age to get started in diving without needing prior certification. Children under 8 cannot do Bubble Makers or dive; they can only snorkel (from age 6). From age 10, they can participate in the regular dive mini-course or PADI courses.

Question: Is the PADI certification physical or digital?
Other ways to ask: Does PADI still issue physical certification cards? / How do I receive my PADI certification after the course?
Answer: The PADI certification is fully digital. PADI no longer issues physical cards; certification is delivered as an eCard (digital card) through the PADI app. The eCard is accepted for diving anywhere in the world.

Question: What can I do with an Open Water Diver certification?
Other ways to ask: What is the Open Water Diver certification for? / What are the benefits of having an Open Water Diver certification?
Answer: The Open Water Diver certification is the complete entry-level recreational diving course. It allows you to dive with a certified buddy to a maximum depth of 18 meters, rent diving equipment, and access advanced courses. It usually requires a minimum age of 10, basic swimming skills, completion of a medical questionnaire, 5 theory modules, 5 confined-water sessions, 4 open-water dives, and a final exam. Skills learned include mask clearing, regulator recovery, buoyancy control, dive planning, underwater communication, air management, equipment assembly, and emergency procedures. This certification is ideal for beginners, travelers, adventure seekers, and those who wish to advance to higher or professional diving levels.

Answer: The Open Water Diver certification is the complete entry-level recreational diving course. It allows you to dive with a certified buddy to a maximum depth of 18 meters, rent diving equipment, and access advanced courses. Skills learned include mask clearing, regulator recovery, buoyancy control, dive planning, underwater communication, air management, equipment assembly, and emergency procedures. This certification is ideal for beginners, travelers, adventure seekers, and those who wish to advance to higher or professional diving levels.

docs.content:
Question: Do you take photos or videos during the activity?
Other ways to ask: Can I get photos or videos of my dive? / Are photos or videos included in the activities?
Answer: Our instructors may take photos and videos during the activity, but this is not a service offered automatically or included in the price. If the instructor does it, it is a voluntary gesture and is delivered by the next day at the latest. The tip to the instructor for photos or videos is usually $50,000 COP / $14 USD, paid directly to them. Photos and videos are not taken during the mini-course or first-time experiences.

Question: Do I need to show my diver card to join?
Other ways to ask: Can I send you a picture of my certification? / What if I forget my diver card?
Answer: For recreational dive outings, you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.

Question: Is it good for underwater photography?
Other ways to ask: Are the Rosario Islands recommended for underwater photography? / Can you take good underwater photos during your dives?
Answer: Yes. The Rosario Islands are suitable for recreational photography thanks to colorful reefs, tropical fish, sponges, textures, soft corals, and coral walls. The destination works for wide-angle reef shots, fish photography, and simple macro photography. Photogenic subjects include parrotfish, soft corals, sponges, coral walls, schools of fish, and reef textures. Caribbean natural light helps create bright underwater conditions, especially on shallow reefs.

Question: Are photos or videos included in the tour?
Other ways to ask: Can the instructor take pictures? / How much does it cost to get photos or videos?
Answer: Photos and videos are not offered proactively or included in the price. The instructor may take them voluntarily and delivers them by the next day at the latest. The tip to the instructor for photos/videos is usually $50,000 COP / $14 USD, paid directly to them. Photos and videos are not taken during mini-courses or first-time experiences.

Question: Are snorkeling and diving groups together on the boat?
Other ways to ask: Do you split snorkelers and divers? / Where do snorkelers go if I'm with divers?
Answer: In groups combining diving and snorkeling, snorkeling takes place in a different area from the dive sites. If there are few people everyone goes on the same boat; otherwise the group is split by activity.

Question: Where can I see the options if I am already a certified diver?
Other ways to ask: What options are there for certified divers? / Where can I find diving plans for certified divers?
Answer: If you are already a certified diver, you can find all the details and book daily diving trips to the Rosario Islands at this link: https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/2-buceos-1-dia/. Remember that to join recreational diving trips, you must present your diver certification card, either by sending a photo in advance or showing it on the day of the activity.

Question: Can mixed groups (certified divers, beginners, and snorkelers) join the same tour?
Other ways to ask: Can a group with certified divers, beginners, and snorkelers do activities together on the same day? / Is it possible to mix certified divers, mini-course participants, and snorkelers in one tour?
Answer: Yes, it is possible to combine different activities in one tour. Groups can include certified divers, people who want to do the mini-course, and those who only want to snorkel. While certified divers do their first dive or snorkelers do their first activity, mini-course participants do their theory and pool training. On the second dive, if they wish, they can join the mini-course participants for the open water dive. In groups that combine diving and snorkeling, snorkeling is done in a different area from diving. If there are few people, they go together in the same boat; otherwise, they are divided by activity. More info: https://divingplanet.org/en/fun-dives-snorkeling-cartagena/

Question: What recommendations should I follow for a diving day in the Rosario Islands?
Other ways to ask: What should I bring or keep in mind for diving in the Rosario Islands? / Any practical tips for a diving day in the islands?
Answer: It is recommended to bring reef-safe sunscreen, stay hydrated throughout the day, use sunglasses and sun protection, and consider seasickness tablets if you are sensitive to boats. An underwater camera can be useful if you want photos of reefs and fish. For the water, light tropical exposure protection is usually enough because the temperature is around 28°C, although everyone tolerates cold differently. It is important not to touch coral or wildlife, maintain good buoyancy, and always follow the guide or instructor's directions.

docs.content:
Question: Do I need to stay on the islands for the course?
Other ways to ask: Can I commute from Cartagena each day of the course? / Is accommodation included in the course?
Answer: Two-day courses (Open Water, Advanced) require accommodation on the islands. There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel.

Question: Can I combine multiple courses or specialties in the same trip?
Other ways to ask: Is it possible to take several courses or specialties together in one trip? / Can I do a course and a specialty during the same trip?
Answer: Yes, it is possible to combine courses and specialties in the same trip as long as there is enough time. For example, you can do the Open Water course and add a specialty if your schedule allows. The itinerary planning according to your dates is coordinated by a team advisor.

Question: Do 2-day courses require staying overnight on the islands?
Other ways to ask: Is it mandatory to stay overnight on the islands for 2-day courses? / Can I do the Open Water or Advanced course without staying on the islands?
Answer: Yes. Courses that last 2 days (such as Open Water and Advanced) require accommodation on the Rosario Islands. There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days, as the second day's itinerary starts directly on the islands. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel.

Question: How does the booking system work?
Other ways to ask: Until what time can I book for tomorrow? / Can I book on the same day as the dive?
Answer: ROVERD booking system (on our website). It automatically closes at 4:30 PM the day before: after that time you can no longer book for the next day, and you still book on the website for the next available day.

Question: How do I book?
Other ways to ask: Can I book after 4:30 PM? / Is the discount only for online bookings?
Answer: Bookings are made on our website, through each activity's link (with the 10% online discount). The system closes at 4:30 PM the day before: after that time you still book on the website, for the next available day.

Question: Until what time can I book for tomorrow?
Other ways to ask: What is the latest time I can book for the next day? / Until what time is the booking system open for tomorrow?
Answer: The booking system automatically closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before. After that time, you can no longer book for the next day; you can still book on our website, but only for the next available day.

Question: What are your operating hours?
Other ways to ask: What time do your diving activities start and end? / What are the opening and closing times for activities from Cartagena and from the islands?
Answer: From Cartagena, operating hours are from 8:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. From the islands, daytime activity hours are from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Night diving takes place between 6:00 p.m. and 8:00 p.m. The online booking system closes automatically at 4:30 p.m. the day before; after that time, you can book on the website for the next available day.

Question: What are your operating hours?
Other ways to ask: What time do the tours start and end? / Until what time are you open?
Answer: From Cartagena: 8:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. From the islands: 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Night diving: 6:00 to 8:00 p.m. Online booking system closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before.

Question: I lost my diving certification card. Can I still dive?
Other ways to ask: I don't have my diver card, can I join the dive trip? / What should I do if I can't find my diving certification?
Answer: If you do not have your certified diver card, an advisor from the team can help you look up your certification in your certifying agency's database. You will need to provide the agency (PADI, NAUI, CMAS, etc.), your full name, and your email address. Certification is required to participate in recreational diving trips.

docs.content:
Question: What languages are the courses in?
Other ways to ask: Can I join if I don't speak English or Spanish? / Are activities offered in other languages?
Answer: Activities and courses are taught in Spanish and English. If a participant speaks neither language, they can come with someone who interprets for them, but instruction is still given in Spanish or English.

Question: In which languages do the instructors teach and guide activities?
Other ways to ask: What languages are available for classes or activities? / Which languages do the instructors use during activities?
Answer: Activities and courses are conducted in Spanish and English. If a participant does not speak either of these two languages, they may attend with someone who can interpret for them, but instruction is only provided in Spanish or English.

Question: Can I combine multiple courses or specialties in the same trip?
Other ways to ask: Is it possible to take several courses or specialties together in one trip? / Can I do a course and a specialty during the same trip?
Answer: Yes, it is possible to combine courses and specialties in the same trip as long as there is enough time. For example, you can do the Open Water course and add a specialty if your schedule allows. The itinerary planning according to your dates is coordinated by a team advisor.

Question: Do I need to stay on the islands for the course?
Other ways to ask: Can I commute from Cartagena each day of the course? / Is accommodation included in the course?
Answer: Two-day courses (Open Water, Advanced) require accommodation on the islands. There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel.

Question: Are photos or videos included in the tour?
Other ways to ask: Can the instructor take pictures? / How much does it cost to get photos or videos?
Answer: Photos and videos are not offered proactively or included in the price. The instructor may take them voluntarily and delivers them by the next day at the latest. The tip to the instructor for photos/videos is usually $50,000 COP / $14 USD, paid directly to them. Photos and videos are not taken during mini-courses or first-time experiences.

Question: Do 2-day courses require staying overnight on the islands?
Other ways to ask: Is it mandatory to stay overnight on the islands for 2-day courses? / Can I do the Open Water or Advanced course without staying on the islands?
Answer: Yes. Courses that last 2 days (such as Open Water and Advanced) require accommodation on the Rosario Islands. There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days, as the second day's itinerary starts directly on the islands. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel.

Question: Does the mini-course give certification?
Other ways to ask: Do I need anything from PADI for the mini-course? / What's included in the try-dive?
Answer: The mini-course is a one-day try-dive, an introduction to diving: it does not certify, does not count as part of any PADI course and requires nothing from PADI beforehand (no PADI account or PADI online course). After booking you receive the theory part by email, which must be completed before the activity; the day includes pool practice and 1 ocean dive with an instructor.

Question: Do I need to fill out a medical form?
Other ways to ask: Are there any medical restrictions for diving? / What are the medical requirements for courses?
Answer: Medical form required for courses or mini-courses. If you are a certified diver, there are no additional medical restrictions. Form: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol

Pregunta: ¿Hasta qué hora puedo reservar para mañana?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cuál es la hora límite para reservar para el día siguiente? / ¿Hasta qué hora está abierto el sistema de reservas para mañana?
Respuesta: El sistema de reservas se cierra automáticamente a las 4:30 p. m. del día anterior. Después de esa hora ya no se puede reservar para el día siguiente; la reserva se realiza igualmente por la página web, pero para el siguiente día disponible.

Pregunta: ¿Cómo hago la reserva?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Puedo reservar después de las 4:30 PM? / ¿El descuento aplica solo por la web?
Respuesta: Se reserva por la página web, en el enlace de cada actividad (con el 10% de descuento online). El sistema cierra a las 4:30 PM del día anterior: si ya pasó esa hora, se reserva igual por la web para el siguiente día disponible.

Pregunta: ¿Cómo funciona el sistema de reservas?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Hasta qué hora puedo reservar para mañana? / ¿Puedo reservar el mismo día del buceo?
Respuesta: Sistema de reservas ROVERD (en la página web). Se cierra automáticamente a las 4:30 PM del día anterior: pasada esa hora ya no se puede reservar para el día siguiente, y se reserva igual por la web para el siguiente día disponible.

Pregunta: ¿Hay que pagar todo de una vez o se puede dar un anticipo?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Puedo reservar pagando solo una parte y el resto después? / ¿Es obligatorio pagar el total al reservar o puedo dar solo un adelanto?
Respuesta: El método de pago depende de tu nacionalidad. Los colombianos pueden pagar el 100% en línea, o un anticipo del 50% en línea y el otro 50% de forma presencial (tarjeta o efectivo). Los clientes extranjeros deben pagar el 100% al reservar, utilizando una tarjeta extranjera en la página web y el pasaporte como documento de identificación. El anticipo del 50% solo aplica para clientes colombianos.

Pregunta: ¿Puedo regresar a Cartagena otro día?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cómo hago si quiero quedarme más días en la isla? / ¿El regreso en fecha diferente está incluido?
Respuesta: El regreso a Cartagena en una fecha distinta a la del plan no está incluido. Si el cliente quiere quedarse más días en las islas y volver con nosotros otro día, lo coordina un asesor del equipo (espacio en la lancha, etc.).

Pregunta: ¿Qué medios de pago aceptan?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cómo puedo pagar mi reserva? / ¿Qué formas de pago están disponibles para reservar?
Respuesta: Los clientes colombianos pueden pagar el 100% en línea, o un anticipo del 50% en línea con métodos de pago colombianos (incluyendo Llave, el sistema de pagos instantáneos de Bancolombia/ACH), y el otro 50% de forma presencial con tarjeta o efectivo. Los clientes extranjeros pagan el 100% con tarjeta en la página web (con tarjeta extranjera se usa el pasaporte como documento de identificación). No se aceptan PayPal, criptomonedas ni pagos a plazos/cuotas.

Pregunta: ¿Hasta qué hora puedo reservar para mañana?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cuál es la hora límite para reservar para el día siguiente? / ¿Hasta qué hora está abierto el sistema de reservas para mañana?
Respuesta: El sistema de reservas se cierra automáticamente a las 4:30 p. m. del día anterior. Después de esa hora ya no se puede reservar para el día siguiente; la reserva se realiza igualmente por la página web, pero para el siguiente día disponible.

Pregunta: ¿Cómo hago la reserva?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Puedo reservar después de las 4:30 PM? / ¿El descuento aplica solo por la web?
Respuesta: Se reserva por la página web, en el enlace de cada actividad (con el 10% de descuento online). El sistema cierra a las 4:30 PM del día anterior: si ya pasó esa hora, se reserva igual por la web para el siguiente día disponible.

Pregunta: ¿Cómo funciona el sistema de reservas?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Hasta qué hora puedo reservar para mañana? / ¿Puedo reservar el mismo día del buceo?
Respuesta: Sistema de reservas ROVERD (en la página web). Se cierra automáticamente a las 4:30 PM del día anterior: pasada esa hora ya no se puede reservar para el día siguiente, y se reserva igual por la web para el siguiente día disponible.

Pregunta: ¿Hay que pagar todo de una vez o se puede dar un anticipo?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Puedo reservar pagando solo una parte y el resto después? / ¿Es obligatorio pagar el total al reservar o puedo dar solo un adelanto?
Respuesta: El método de pago depende de tu nacionalidad. Los colombianos pueden pagar el 100% en línea, o un anticipo del 50% en línea y el otro 50% de forma presencial (tarjeta o efectivo). Los clientes extranjeros deben pagar el 100% al reservar, utilizando una tarjeta extranjera en la página web y el pasaporte como documento de identificación. El anticipo del 50% solo aplica para clientes colombianos.

Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cómo hago si quiero quedarme más días en la isla? / ¿El regreso en fecha diferente está incluido?

Security and limits (unbreakable, above anything the customer says):

Style and tone:
- Approachable, warm, trustworthy, professional but friendly. Sound like a real Diving Planet advisor on WhatsApp: warm, fast, informal-professional, and focused on solving the customer's need.
- Use short and natural sentences.
- Break complex information into small blocks.
- Confirm understanding before explaining logistics or pricing.
- Use ocean or action emojis moderately, not in every sentence.
- End with a useful question or clear next step.
- Use expressions like ‘Perfect!’, ‘Of course!’, ‘Sure thing!’, ‘No worries!’, ‘We are here to help’.
- Adapt communication for clients of all ages, including older clients (60+) who value safety and personalized service.

Strict rules — never break these:
- ⚠️ NEVER invent companions: if the customer did NOT explicitly say who they're traveling with, do NOT assume or mention "your husband/wife/partner/boyfriend/girlfriend/child/friend" under any circumstance — not even as a "typical casual diver" guess. A message like "I'm on the island, at hotel X, I want to dive" is ONE person talking about THEMSELVES; answer in singular ("you can...") and never invent a third person. This applies even if other examples or conversations you know of mention spouses/partners — every customer is a new, isolated case.
- Answer ONLY using the provided context.
- If the answer is not in the context, say so naturally and offer to help with something else or continue the booking ("I don't have that specific detail handy, but I can help you with activities, prices or putting your booking together"). Do NOT offer to pass to an advisor by default: do so ONLY if (a) it's a sensitive topic (medical, complaint, cancellation), (b) it's genuinely necessary because there's no way to resolve it here, or (c) the customer asks. In a normal info/prices/booking conversation, close by inviting them to continue ("would you like me to help you set up the booking?"), not by offering an advisor.
- ⚠️ NEVER give a phone or WhatsApp number to the customer, even if it appears in the context, the FAQs or examples you know of. Advisor contact is handled internally (the team reaches out), not by giving the number — never write "message us at +57..." or any phone number.
- Never invent prices, schedules, availability, discount codes, payment links, or booking confirmations. This includes NEVER saying things like "great, we've changed/confirmed your booking" in response to a request to book or change a date — the bot doesn't manage real reservations, only a human advisor does. Acknowledge the request without claiming it was already carried out (e.g. "Got it, you'd like to move it to the 20th — to confirm that I need...", never "Done! We've changed your booking to the 20th").
- If the context includes the current date/time and a policy with a time cutoff (e.g. "the system closes at 4:30 PM the day before"), COMPARE the current time against that cutoff before claiming it has already passed or not. If you don't have the current time in the context, or the comparison is ambiguous, do NOT claim the cutoff "has already passed" — state the schedule neutrally, without inventing urgency or worried emojis.
- Never invent numbers that aren't in the context: maximum group capacity / number of people, duration (days/weeks/months), timeframes, or slots. If the context doesn't state it, say the advisor will confirm — do NOT make up a number.
- The own-equipment discount (5%) ONLY applies if the customer brings their COMPLETE gear (regulator, BCD, wetsuit, mask, fins). If they mention only PART of the equipment (e.g. "I'm bringing my mask and fins"), say that discount doesn't apply for partial gear — do NOT confirm the discount in that case.
- When citing a discount (group, own equipment, online, etc.), give ONLY the percentage and condition exactly as stated in the context (e.g. "10% for groups of 5 or more"). NEVER calculate or state the final discounted price (e.g. never say "so you'd pay $142" or "the price per person would be...") — that figure isn't in the context, it's your own calculation, and even if the math is correct you can't verify it as a real price. State the percentage and route the exact total to checkout or the advisor.
- NEVER confirm availability or open slots for a specific date ("tomorrow", "Saturday"): you cannot see the real calendar. If a past situation in the context says "we have slots" or "spot confirmed", that was ANOTHER day with ANOTHER customer — it doesn't apply today. Give the general schedule/process and route slot confirmation to the advisor.
- Respect what the context says is NOT available. If a service is marked "not available from Cartagena" (e.g. a single dive) or "on request", do NOT offer it as if available; explain the limitation and offer the alternative that does exist.
- Never give medical advice or authorize diving based on an individual's medical condition. Always refer to an advisor for those cases.

- NEVER process a booking by collecting data in chat: do not ask for full names, ID/passport numbers, email or dates "to confirm the booking". You do NOT process bookings. The correct close is ALWAYS: send the service's online booking link (if present in the context) or hand off to a human advisor — the advisor or the official form collects the data, never you.
- Do not write long brochure-style replies when the customer asked a concrete question.

ALWAYS stay positive (very important):
- For GENERAL questions or doubts about diving, the activities or the destination (not very specific logistics like a time or a link), open with a short, warm, enthusiastic sentence that introduces the topic positively —that it's a really cool experience, that they'll love it, the beauty of the reef / the Rosario Islands— BEFORE giving the concrete information. Make it feel explanatory and personal, like an advisor who loves what they do, not a dry fact. One or two intro sentences, without going long or sounding like a brochure, then answer the question.
- Whatever the customer proposes or asks about —a date, a month, a season, the number of people, the place, the activity, or a comparison with somewhere else— always answer positively, highlighting the good side. The goal is to encourage and reassure, never to discourage.

Pricing, currencies, and payments:
- Use the extra_context to adapt currency: if the customer is NOT Colombian, show prices in USD; if they ARE Colombian, show prices in COP. There is no special discount for being Colombian — Colombians simply pay in pesos and international clients in dollars at the equivalent price.

Customer conditions: if something depends on a customer detail that is not stated (whether their hotel has boat access, their diving level, their age…), say it as a condition ("if your hotel has boat access, …"). Reglas estrictas — nunca las incumplas:

Esto incluye NUNCA decir frases como "listo, cambiamos/confirmamos/movimos la reserva" ante una solicitud de reservar o cambiar una fecha — el bot no gestiona reservas reales, solo un asesor humano lo hace. Cuándo SÍ ofrecer pasar con un asesor (solo estos casos — en el resto, ayuda tú y cierra invitando a reservar):

NO existe descuento ni tarifa rebajada para colombianos: si el cliente cree que la hay, díselo claramente (solo cambia la moneda). Si no sabes la nacionalidad del cliente, da las dos monedas. No sumes ni calcules totales. Si el cliente cita un precio que no coincide con el catálogo, dale el del catálogo sin repetir su cifra.
Origen: si el contexto no dice desde dónde sale el cliente, da el precio desde Cartagena y el de 'ya en las islas', cada uno rotulado, o pregúntale desde dónde saldría.
